title: First and second derivatives of √h(t) at a point where h = 1 (derivative form of √(1 + x) = 1 + x/2 − x²/8 + O(x³))
statement: Let h : ℝ → ℝ satisfy h(0) = 1, and suppose h has derivative h₁ at 0. (1) Then t ↦ √h(t) has derivative h₁/2 at 0. (2) Suppose moreover that h is differentiable at every point of some neighbourhood of 0 and that the function deriv h has derivative h₂ at 0. Then the function deriv(t ↦ √h(t)) has derivative h₂/2 − h₁²/4 at 0. Here √ is Real.sqrt.
lean_statement: ∀ (h : ℝ → ℝ) (h₁ : ℝ), h 0 = 1 → HasDerivAt h h₁ 0 → HasDerivAt (fun t ↦ Real.sqrt (h t)) (h₁ / 2) 0 ∧ ∀ h₂ : ℝ, (∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 0, DifferentiableAt ℝ h t) → HasDerivAt (deriv h) h₂ 0 → HasDerivAt (deriv (fun t ↦ Real.sqrt (h t))) (h₂ / 2 - h₁ ^ 2 / 4) 0
